title: GPT generated player sprites with rayman style hands to reduce token usage.
author: RoyalSpecialist1777
selftext:
Just wanted to show off the player sprites we ended up with.  This is three of them out of 20 so far for our bug farming game.  

Using rayman style hands (floating hands) means we only have to generate the sprites for the walking animations and gauntlets.  All the tool swings are then done via code.  

It is a relatively standard pipeline: we use gpt-image-2 to create the sprites with a magenta background that is cropped out, prompt techniques are used to create sprites with high consistency from our naked reference sprite, and then we use a pipeline to align and then convert to actual pixels.

It needs some cleanup but I am ok with that.

comments.author: Curious-Thanks3966
comments.body: Looks awesome! Did you generate each animation cycle with an individual prompt, or did you prompt a full sprite sheet containing multiple animations at once? I'd also love to learn a bit about your prompting technique!

replies.author: RoyalSpecialist1777
replies.body:
I generated a reference image of the player sprite facing the camera wearing armor using a reference image of the player sprite in underwear.  I actually generate 3 and choose from them.  From this I used the one I like and generated the entire sprite sheet with the sprite facing different directions and with different walking positions.  We then crop each individual sprite out.  There is more to it, it took days iterating to get it down, but that is the gist.

This biggest trick involves language you use which gets the image model to enter into specific modes.  In this case you can't just say 'hey give me a version of this guy wearing armor' but rather use explicit 'minimum difference' language so it shifts to preserving features rather than just making something similar.  

https://preview.redd.it/zhe5n0hqx6jh1.png?width=36&format=png&auto=webp&s=540738bcf739c8e68c5382458ad55a240d0b7660

This is what I start with.  I generated this with GPT and then redid the face as I dont like their default faces and no matter what 'make it more like SNES sprites' I did they couldn't do it.  I find it is good to know some editing skills as it helps a lot.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: If you'r eusing rayman style hands, consider separating your animations. Consider posing the character's body separately from the hands and use an attachment point for a weapon sprite that isn't baked into the sheet. This allows you to have a character able to walk or run while swinging a sword/mallet whatever. And then you also don't need separate animations for the sword/mallet (or any variations of them). You just have the hand and character sprite appropriately overlaid, then the weapon attachment point which tells the engine "weapon swings in this arc" and uses a rigged, reusable keyframe based animation. Other advantages to this are being able to do something like this are being able to scale up just the weapon/hands during the swing to sell the anticipation and follow through.
